_comment: Coils of the polarized NH3 target magnet in the Oxford Instruments 2012 design study for SoLID: a split pair
of 7 superconducting coils per side on a common axis, with a +-25 deg opening and 5 T at the centre.
The numbers are those of solid_gemc/field/oxford_field.f (subroutine sda_ptf_solid_nh3, C. Gu): arrays RI, RA,
ZAU, ZBU, TURNS and the current CURm; the first pair is wound in the opposite sense (RJ(1), RJ(2) negative
there, negative turns here). oxford_field.f made the GEMC map oxford_ptarget.dat (r 0..199 cm, axis -200..200
cm, values rounded to 0.1 G); coil_map.py reproduces it and writes the same field out to any distance.
z is the coordinate along the magnet axis, r the distance from it, both in the magnet frame (origin at the
target centre). In the hall the magnet axis is the x axis (transverse polarization): "axis": "x".
No iron: the yoke of the SoLID solenoid is not part of this calculation.
name: nh3_target_oxford2012
source: solid_gemc/field/oxford_field.f (Oxford Instruments 2012 design study, C. Gu)
